text:
Leaching of unconsolidated overburden will affect ground water quality to the base of the Robinson coal, and consequently, springs receiving recharge from the mined area. This will be particularly true where an unmined buffer of consolidated rock and/or dilution effects of water from other sources are not present. Increases in alkalinity, dissolved solids including sulfates, bicarbonate and alkaline earth metals are the most probable effects. Limited effects of such spring discharge on water quality in major streams may be expected, but should not be significant because of the small quantities of water involved.
Decreases in quality of ground water due to leaching will be largely confined to the lease area since the affected aquifers outcrop within or very near the tract boundaries. Limited recharge to quaternary alluvium in the valleys of Sarpy and East Sarpy Creeks may occur as a result of infiltration of spring flow.
Sanitary landfills, sewage treatment facilities, and septic tanks in or around mining areas of Tracts II and III may permanently affect water quality. However, if the sites were selected properly, and adequate operation and control of the site has been enforced, no serious after effects should be observed.
Sediment ponds which are used for detaining sediment and mine drainage runoff may have future uses as stock watering ponds or irrigation water sources. Sediment would have to be removed and approval for their use as water sources would have to be obtained from appropriate State and Federal agencies.
